title: Managing Change
summary: How to lead a team through organisational change, new supervisory approaches or technology, understand reactions to change and keep the team focused and engaged.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to lead a team through organisational change, new supervisory approaches or technology, understand reactions to change and keep the team focused and engaged.
Learning Objectives: Explain how people respond to change and why change initiatives fail
Communicate the case for change and involve the team
Plan and sustain the implementation of change in the team
Syllabus: Why change happens in supervisory authorities
Reactions to change and managing resistance
Communicating and involving the team in change
Embedding change: quick wins, feedback and follow-through
Intended Audience: Supervisors newly promoted, or preparing for promotion, into team leader and manager roles
Managers and heads of department in supervisory authorities seeking to strengthen their leadership
Technical specialists who lead projects, thematic reviews or cross-functional teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience in a supervisory or technical role is helpful. No prior management training is required.
Core Reading: Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Patrick Lencioni, The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (2002)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
